newsitem.title: UK: Euro Products Outlook - Little impetus for rises.
newsitem.headline: Euro Products Outlook - Little impetus for rises.

text.p: European oil products look shaky for the next few days despite gains last week, traders said.
Gasoline has no trans-Atlantic arb opportunity, naphtha has dull demand, fuel looks flat and gas oil is beset by bearish imports.
Gasoline is expected to be volatile as traders balance buying by one U.S.-based firm in the ARA barge market with a shut arbitrage to the U.S.
"The fundamentals are not bullish anymore," said a trader at a large European oil company. "I don't see the barges as tight."
The spread between premium unleaded and regular unleaded barges could widen out toward $10 from about $5-$7, he said, citing the closed arbitrage and unsold cargoes of regular.
Some dealers questioned last week's strength, suggesting it was related to a long swaps position, although other dealers argued supplies of Rotterdam refinery material were tight.
Med gasoline prices are expected to stay firm after Turkey's tender last week and light West African demand.
Naphtha looks set to trade sideways as anaemic end-user demand offsets recent trader buying.

"I think the arb is definitely closed (from the Med to Asia) even though some think it might reopen," a trader said. "I think more Med tonnage will end up in Northwest Europe and may put liquidity in the market."

The trader, who works at one of the largest end-users in Northwest Europe, said Japan had not seen as much material from the Med recently. The backwardation in June/July swaps, which widened out to $3-$4 last week, may narrow towards parity.
Some London sources, however, said naphtha's fundamentals had moved from a negative tone to a more positive one.
"It was slightly long to bearish and now it's slightly short to bullish...There are fewer cargoes from the 20th (of June) to the fifth of July," a broker said.
High sulphur fuel barges should be able to hold around $86/87 for the first part of this week on short-lifting and crude's firmer tone, traders said.
Views were mixed about high sulphur fuel oil cargoes, with some traders saying they will be steady to a shade firmer with most prompt cargoes committed.
Others saw it balanced to weaker with the market sapped by people bidding floating prices instead of fixed prices.

Low sulphur will continue to be quiet with $91/93 seen as a range. In the Mediterranean, the outlook was bearish for high sulphur fuel oil with three or four prompt cargoes still looking for homes after an M-100 cargo traded at a distressed $83.25 cif Med.
"There is no demand, this will put pressure on prices next week," one trader said.
There were few signs the gas oil market would be able to lift itself out of its recent doldrums with lacklustre demand and continuing heavy exports into the area expected.

Heating oil barges were extremely weak on Friday with price differentials to the IPE July gas oil contract quoted at -50 cents/+50 cents fob ARA, while low sulphur premiums were approaching record lows with material offered at +$5.00 fob ARA.

Some traders said 0.05 percent premiums were approaching levels which might encourage refiners to scale back low sulphur production, although others said this would do little to alleviate the length in the market.
"I can't see it getting much better," one trader said. "Even if refiners scaled back production, imports would keep supplies on the long side." -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8980
